passages.text: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Saul was the son of Kish.
Saul was king over Israel.
Samuel said, “The LORD sent me.
The LORD told me to anoint you.
You are king over His people.
His people are Israel.
Now listen to the words of the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל אֹתִ֨י שָׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ לִמְשָׁחֳךָ֣ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ עַל־ עַמּ֖וֹ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֣ה שְׁמַ֔ע לְק֖וֹל דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they ambushed them on their way up from Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts spoke.
The LORD of Hosts is the God who commands armies.
The LORD of Hosts said, “I saw what the Amalekites did to Israel.
The Amalekites attacked the Israelites.
They ambushed Israel on the road.
This happened when Israel came up from Egypt.”
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת פָּקַ֕דְתִּי אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה עֲמָלֵ֖ק לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר־ שָׂ֥ם לוֹ֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בַּעֲלֹת֖וֹ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Saul through Samuel.
God commanded Saul to attack the Amalekites.
God told Saul to destroy everything that belongs to the Amalekites.
God said, “Do not spare them.”
God commanded Saul to kill every man and every woman.
God commanded Saul to kill every child and every infant.
God commanded Saul to kill every ox and every sheep.
God commanded Saul to kill every camel and every donkey.
passages.original: עַתָּה֩ לֵ֨ךְ וְהִכִּֽיתָ֜ה אֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֗ק וְהַֽחֲרַמְתֶּם֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ל עָלָ֑יו וְהֵמַתָּ֞ה מֵאִ֣ישׁ עַד־ אִשָּׁ֗ה מֵֽעֹלֵל֙ וְעַד־ יוֹנֵ֔ק מִשּׁ֣וֹר וְעַד־ שֶׂ֔ה מִגָּמָ֖ל וְעַד־ חֲמֽוֹר׃ס

passages.text: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul called the people together.
He gathered the troops at a place called Telaim.
He counted the soldiers.
There were 200,000 foot soldiers.
There were also 10,000 men from Judah.
passages.original: וַיְשַׁמַּ֤ע שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּפְקְדֵם֙ בַּטְּלָאִ֔ים מָאתַ֥יִם אֶ֖לֶף רַגְלִ֑י וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים אֶת־ אִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul led his army to the city of Amalek.
He arrived at the city of Amalek.
Saul waited in the valley near the city.
He prepared to attack the Amalekites.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל עַד־ עִ֣יר עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיָּ֖רֶב בַּנָּֽחַל׃

passages.text: And he warned the Kenites, “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away with them.” So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to the Kenites.
The Kenites were living among the Amalekites.
Saul said, “Go away from the Amalekites.
Leave them now.
If you stay, I might destroy you with them.
You showed kindness to all the Israelites.
You helped the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.”
The Kenites left the Amalekites.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֣וּל אֶֽל־ הַקֵּינִ֡י לְכוּ֩ סֻּ֨רוּ רְד֜וּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ עֲמָלֵקִ֗י פֶּן־ אֹֽסִפְךָ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֞ה עָשִׂ֤יתָה חֶ֙סֶד֙ עִם־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּעֲלוֹתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֥סַר קֵינִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ עֲמָלֵֽק׃

passages.text: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul attacked the Amalekites.
He defeated them from Havilah to Shur.
Shur is east of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥ךְ שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֑ק מֵֽחֲוִילָה֙ בּוֹאֲךָ֣ שׁ֔וּר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the others to destruction with the sword.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul fought against the Amalekites.
Saul captured Agag.
Agag was the king of Amalek.
Saul kept Agag alive.
Saul killed all the other Amalekite people with the sword.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפֹּ֛שׂ אֶת־ אֲגַ֥ג מֶֽלֶךְ־ עֲמָלֵ֖ק חָ֑י וְאֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם הֶחֱרִ֥ים לְפִי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to destroy them, but they devoted to destruction all that was despised and worthless.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
He led his people in battle against the Amalekites.
Saul and his troops captured Agag.
Agag was the king of Amalek.
They spared Agag’s life.
They also spared the best sheep.
They spared the best cattle.
They spared the fat calves.
They spared the lambs.
They spared everything that was good.
Saul and his troops did not want to destroy these things.
They refused to destroy them.
They destroyed only what was despised.
They destroyed only what was worthless.
passages.original: וַיַּחְמֹל֩ שָׁא֨וּל וְהָעָ֜ם עַל־ אֲגָ֗ג וְעַל־ מֵיטַ֣ב הַצֹּאן֩ וְהַבָּקָ֨ר וְהַמִּשְׁנִ֤ים וְעַל־ הַכָּרִים֙ וְעַל־ כָּל־ הַטּ֔וֹב וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וּ הַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְכָל־ הַמְּלָאכָ֛ה נְמִבְזָ֥ה וְנָמֵ֖ס אֹתָ֥הּ הֶחֱרִֽימוּ׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying, “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.” And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Samuel.
God said, “I regret making Saul king.
Saul has turned away from Me.
Saul has not obeyed My commands.”
Samuel became very upset.
Samuel cried out to God all night.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹֽר׃ נִחַ֗מְתִּי כִּֽי־ הִמְלַ֤כְתִּי אֶת־ שָׁאוּל֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ שָׁב֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְאֶת־ דְּבָרַ֖י לֹ֣א הֵקִ֑ים וַיִּ֙חַר֙ לִשְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּזְעַ֥ק אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה כָּל־ הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Early in the morning, Samuel got up.
Samuel wanted to meet Saul.
Someone told Samuel, “Saul has gone to Carmel.”
Saul set up a monument for himself in Carmel.
Then Saul left Carmel.
Saul went down to Gilgal.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֧ם שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל לִקְרַ֥את שָׁא֖וּל בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִשְׁמוּאֵ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּֽא־ שָׁא֤וּל הַכַּרְמֶ֙לָה֙ וְהִנֵּ֨ה מַצִּ֥יב לוֹ֙ יָ֔ד וַיִּסֹּב֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔ר וַיֵּ֖רֶד הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

passages.text: When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel came to Saul.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said, “May the LORD bless you.”
Saul said, “I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל־ שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ שָׁא֗וּל בָּר֤וּךְ אַתָּה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הֲקִימֹ֖תִי אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel said, “I hear the sound of sheep in my ears.
I also hear the sound of cattle.
Why do I hear these animals?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וּמֶ֛ה קֽוֹל־ הַצֹּ֥אן הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאָזְנָ֑י וְק֣וֹל הַבָּקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: Saul answered, “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said the troops brought animals from the Amalekites.
The people spared the best sheep and cattle.
They wanted to sacrifice these animals to the LORD, your God.
We destroyed all the other animals.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל מֵעֲמָלֵקִ֣י הֱבִיא֗וּם אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָמַ֤ל הָעָם֙ עַל־ מֵיטַ֤ב הַצֹּאן֙ וְהַבָּקָ֔ר לְמַ֥עַן זְבֹ֖חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְאֶת־ הַיּוֹתֵ֖ר הֶחֱרַֽמְנוּ׃ס

passages.text: “Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” “Tell me,” Saul replied.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Samuel spoke to Saul, the king of Israel.
Samuel said, “Stop.”
Samuel said, “I will tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”
Saul replied, “Tell me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל הֶ֚רֶף וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לְּךָ֔ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ ל֖וֹ דַּבֵּֽר׃ס

passages.text: And Samuel said, “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Saul was once small in his own eyes.
Now Saul is the head of the tribes of Israel.
The LORD chose Saul.
The LORD anointed Saul as king over Israel.
The LORD sent Saul on a mission.
The LORD commanded Saul to destroy the sinful Amalekites.
The LORD told Saul to fight against the Amalekites until he wiped them out.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל הֲל֗וֹא אִם־ קָטֹ֤ן אַתָּה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ רֹ֛אשׁ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אָ֑תָּה וַיִּמְשָׁחֲךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיִּשְׁלָחֲךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה בְּדָ֑רֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֣ךְ וְהַחֲרַמְתָּ֞ה אֶת־ הַֽחַטָּאִים֙ אֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וְנִלְחַמְתָּ֣ ב֔וֹ עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתָ֖ם אֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel asked Saul a question.
Samuel said, “Why did you not obey the LORD?”
Samuel said, “You rushed to take the plunder.”
Samuel said, “You did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.”
passages.original: וְלָ֥מָּה לֹא־ שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וַתַּ֙עַט֙ אֶל־ הַשָּׁלָ֔ל וַתַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said, “I obeyed the LORD.
I listened to the LORD’s voice.
I went on the mission the LORD sent me on.
I brought back Agag.
Agag is the king of Amalek.
I destroyed the people of Amalek.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וָאֵלֵ֕ךְ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה וָאָבִ֗יא אֶת־ אֲגַג֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וְאֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֖ק הֶחֱרַֽמְתִּי׃

passages.text: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
passages.sermon:
The people took animals from the plunder.
They took sheep and cattle.
They chose the best animals.
These animals were supposed to be destroyed.
The people wanted to offer these animals as sacrifices.
They planned to sacrifice them to the LORD your God.
They wanted to do this at Gilgal.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח הָעָ֧ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֛ל צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר רֵאשִׁ֣ית הַחֵ֑רֶם לִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בַּגִּלְגָּֽל׃

passages.text: But Samuel declared: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel asked a question about God’s desire.
Samuel said, “Does the LORD want burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as He wants people to obey His voice?”
Samuel explained what God values most.
Samuel said, “Obeying God is better than offering a sacrifice.”
Samuel said, “Listening to God is better than giving the fat of rams.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל הַחֵ֤פֶץ לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּעֹל֣וֹת וּזְבָחִ֔ים כִּשְׁמֹ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה שְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ מִזֶּ֣בַח ט֔וֹב לְהַקְשִׁ֖יב מֵחֵ֥לֶב אֵילִֽים׃

passages.text: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel said, “Rebellion is like the sin of divination.
Arrogance is like the evil of idolatry.
You have rejected the word of the LORD.
Therefore, the LORD has rejected you as king.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י חַטַּאת־ קֶ֙סֶם֙ מֶ֔רִי וְאָ֥וֶן וּתְרָפִ֖ים הַפְצַ֑ר יַ֗עַן מָאַ֙סְתָּ֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּמְאָסְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said, “I have sinned.”
Saul said, “I disobeyed the command of the LORD.”
Saul said, “I did not follow your instructions.”
Saul said, “I was afraid of the people.”
Saul said, “I listened to their voice.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֤וּל אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵל֙ חָטָ֔אתִי כִּֽי־ עָבַ֥רְתִּי אֶת־ פִּֽי־ יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ דְּבָרֶ֑יךָ כִּ֤י יָרֵ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had sinned against the LORD.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said, “Please forgive my sin.
Return with me.
I want to worship the LORD.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֕ה שָׂ֥א נָ֖א אֶת־ חַטָּאתִ֑י וְשׁ֣וּב עִמִּ֔י וְאֶֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel said, “I will not return with you.”
Samuel said, “You have rejected the word of the LORD.”
Samuel said, “The LORD has rejected you as king over Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל לֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב עִמָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מָאַ֙סְתָּה֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּמְאָסְךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה מִהְי֥וֹת מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the hem of his robe, and it tore.
passages.sermon: Samuel turned to leave.\r\nSaul grabbed the edge of Samuel’s robe.\r\nThe robe tore.
passages.original: וַיִּסֹּ֥ב שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל לָלֶ֑כֶת וַיַּחֲזֵ֥ק בִּכְנַף־ מְעִיל֖וֹ וַיִּקָּרַֽע׃

passages.text: So Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel said, “The LORD has taken the kingdom of Israel away from you today.
The LORD has given the kingdom to your neighbor.
Your neighbor is better than you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל קָרַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־ מַמְלְכ֧וּת יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵעָלֶ֖יךָ הַיּ֑וֹם וּנְתָנָ֕הּ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ הַטּ֥וֹב מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.”
passages.sermon:
God is the Glory of Israel.
God never lies.
God never changes His mind.
God is not a man.
God does not change His mind like a man.
passages.original: וְגַם֙ נֵ֣צַח יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א יְשַׁקֵּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יִנָּחֵ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א אָדָ֛ם ה֖וּא לְהִנָּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: “I have sinned,” Saul replied. “Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Samuel.
Saul said, “I have sinned.”
Saul asked Samuel to honor him now.
Saul wanted honor in front of the elders of his people.
Saul wanted honor in front of all Israel.
Saul asked Samuel to return with him.
Saul wanted to worship the LORD, Samuel’s God.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חָטָ֔אתִי עַתָּ֗ה כַּבְּדֵ֥נִי נָ֛א נֶ֥גֶד זִקְנֵֽי־ עַמִּ֖י וְנֶ֣גֶד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשׁ֣וּב עִמִּ֔י וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֖יתִי לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel went back with Saul.
Saul worshiped the LORD.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥שָׁב שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ שָׁא֖וּל לַֽיהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then Samuel said, “Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites.” Agag came to him cheerfully, for he thought, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Samuel spoke with authority from God.
Samuel said, “Bring me Agag, king of the Amalekites.”
Agag was the king of the Amalekites.
Agag came to Samuel.
Agag came in a cheerful manner.
Agag thought, “Surely the bitterness of death has passed.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל הַגִּ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־ אֲגַג֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֵלָ֔יו אֲגַ֖ג מַעֲדַנֹּ֑ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲגָ֔ג אָכֵ֖ן סָ֥ר מַר־ הַמָּֽוֶת׃ס

passages.text: But Samuel declared: “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.” And Samuel hacked Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Agag was the king of the Amalekites.
Samuel spoke to Agag.
Samuel said, “Your sword made many women lose their children.
Now your mother will lose her child among women.”
Samuel killed Agag at Gilgal.
Samuel did this before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שִׁכְּלָ֤ה נָשִׁים֙ חַרְבֶּ֔ךָ כֵּן־ תִּשְׁכַּ֥ל מִנָּשִׁ֖ים אִמֶּ֑ךָ וַיְשַׁסֵּ֨ף שְׁמוּאֵ֧ל אֶת־ אֲגָ֛ג לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בַּגִּלְגָּֽל׃ס

passages.text: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Samuel left the place where he was.
Samuel went to Ramah.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul left the place where he was.
Saul went up to his home.
Saul’s home was in Gibeah of Saul.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הָרָמָ֑תָה וְשָׁא֛וּל עָלָ֥ה אֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel never saw Saul again until Samuel died.
Samuel mourned for Saul.
The LORD regretted making Saul king over Israel.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ יָסַ֨ף שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל לִרְא֤וֹת אֶת־ שָׁאוּל֙ עַד־ י֣וֹם מוֹת֔וֹ כִּֽי־ הִתְאַבֵּ֥ל שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל־ שָׁא֑וּל וַיהוָ֣ה נִחָ֔ם כִּֽי־ הִמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת־ שָׁא֖וּל עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
